sources.title: Nikunj Saunshi et al., A Theoretical Analysis of Contrastive Unsupervised Representation Learning
sources.locator: Full 10-page PMLR paper read; inspected §§2–6, Definitions 2.1–2.3, Theorems 4.1/4.5, Lemmas 4.2–4.4, Lemma 5.1 and Corollary 5.1.1. The full text and relevant arguments were read.

contents.name: §2, Definitions 2.1–2.3: mean classifier, average supervised loss, and one-negative unsupervised loss
contents.reason: The local definition carries the latent-class, positive-pair, marginal-negative, binary-task, mean-classifier, and one-negative loss conventions explicitly.

contents.name: §3, overview of the main contrastive transfer results
contents.reason: The informal overview is absorbed into the local formal transfer theorem, whose exact hypotheses and constants are proved from the detailed results in §4.

contents.name: §4.1, Theorem 4.1 and Lemma 4.2: empirical-minimizer transfer and uniform generalization route
contents.reason: The local empirical-minimizer lemma proves the population excess comparison from the explicit uniform deviation bound and retains selector measurability and optimization tolerance.

contents.name: §4.1, Lemma 4.3: Jensen comparison with the average mean-classifier loss
contents.reason: The local proof gives the conditioning, Jensen step, uniform-label average, and ordered-pair symmetry argument in full.

contents.name: §4.2, Equation (8), Lemma 4.4 and Theorem 4.5: class-collision decomposition, within-class deviation and transfer
contents.reason: The local collision lemma derives the covariance bound and the local transfer theorem keeps both the collision probability and covariance penalty visible.

contents.name: §5.1, Figure 1(b): high within-class variance despite a zero-risk mean classifier
contents.reason: The local finite example computes both collision branches exactly and verifies the qualitative failure mode shown in the paper.

contents.name: §5.1, Figure 1(a): a representation with a poor mean classifier despite a good task-specific linear direction
contents.reason: This separate mean-classifier failure mode is not one of the assigned examples; the batch includes the collision, variance, augmentation, empirical projection-head, and loss-scope examples instead.

contents.name: §5.2, Lemma 5.1 and Corollary 5.1.1: sub-Gaussian margin comparison and transfer
contents.reason: The local lemma preserves the exact piecewise margin parameter and the local corollary restricts the source margin route to hinge loss.

contents.name: §6, multiple-negative and block-similarity extensions
contents.reason: The assigned model has one independent marginal negative and the source treats multiple negatives and block losses as separate extensions requiring different sampling and collision arguments.

contents.name: Appendix A.1: full covariance expansion and class-collision deviation proof
contents.reason: The local proof expands the centered independent class-conditional vectors and derives the square-root-two covariance constant directly.

contents.name: Appendix A.2: full proof of Lemma 5.1, including the sub-Gaussian tail and piecewise margin parameter
contents.reason: The local derivation reproduces the tail scale, epsilon over R-squared bound, bounded-score error, and class-pair averaging, while making the hinge-loss scope explicit.

contents.name: Appendix A.3: bounded-loss generalization and vector-contraction proof route
contents.reason: The local uniform bound normalizes by the exact loss oscillation and proves its own finite-dimensional vector-contraction step.

contents.name: Appendix A.4: Jensen comparison for a block-similarity objective
contents.reason: The block-similarity objective changes the loss grouping; this batch proves only the source one-negative triplet objective and does not import the block-loss comparison.
